articles.title: Sebi bets on trading reforms to reverse  foreign capital flight
articles.content: India's market regulator is poised to introduce substantial rule amendments aimed at boosting foreign investments. The planned reforms intend to lower collateral demands and stimulate interest in longer-term derivatives. With foreign investment in Indian stocks hitting a seventeen-year low, the Securities and Exchange Board of India will engage with industry players prior to rolling out these transformative measures, ultimately hoping to enhance India's position in global stock market rankings.

articles.title: Gold hovers near early-June high on lower bond yields
articles.content: Gold prices soared close to a two-month peak on Thursday after the U.S. Treasury announced bolstered liquidity measures. With yields falling and the dollar weakening, gold became increasingly attractive to investors. This move comes in light of persistent inflation fears and looming interest rate hikes, highlighting gold's reputation as a secure haven during times of financial instability.

articles.title: Dollar hugs three-month lows as Treasury seeks to sooth the bond market
articles.content: On Thursday, the U.S. dollar faced notable declines, approaching its lowest point in three months. In a bid to stabilize the bond market, U.S. Treasury disclosed plans to double its buyback operations. Meanwhile, long-end Treasury yields fell from a nineteen-year peak. Meeting minutes from the Federal Reserve underscored concerns about inflation and possible interest rate hikes. The Japanese yen also retreated from the 160 mark versus the dollar.

articles.title: Oil prices steady as investors assess US-Iran war outlook
articles.content: Oil prices stabilized as market participants evaluated the potential implications of the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict. Shipping activity in the Strait of Hormuz faced disruptions due to rising tensions in the region. Last week's data revealed an increase in crude and gasoline inventories in the United States. Heightened volatility from conflicts in the Middle East continues to support market dynamics, suggesting a steady upward trajectory in oil prices.

articles.title: Rupee falls to a 3-week low of 95.71, raising financial concerns
articles.content: The Indian rupee closed at a three-week low of 95.75 on Wednesday. Substantial central bank interventions prevented further losses for the local currency. Indian equity indices also fell, reflecting the impact of soaring energy costs.
